evidence: Sets f_15CC = 0 / f_15CE = 1, then f_15CC = (0x002F265C() == 2) - i.e. the screen count decides which screen block is active (f_15CC is used as the block selector in 0x1D1F14/0x1D2ADC/0x1D2F64). Calls 0x001D22D0, 0x001D1B60, 0x001D22D0 and 0x001D4DA4, all in this batch.

name: maybe_Gfx_StartPendingView
summary: Starts the pending view change: when the global timer passed the stored deadline it switches the active view and clears the request; also runs the row-layout default when the flag is set.
evidence: Compares *(g_001D1B58+self) with self->f_4C, sets f_50 = 1 and f_15D4 = f_44, then calls 0x001D15F4 when the byte at g_001D1B5C+self is set; ends by setting f_29 = 1, f_28 = 0.

name: Gfx_ResetScreenViews
signature: void Gfx_ResetScreenViews(void* self, unsigned int viewId, char* mode)
summary: Resets both 3DS screen view blocks and their view entries, re-applies the default view and initialises the layout state for the given mode.
evidence: Calls 0x00622C30 on both screen blocks at +0x54 and +0xB10 (the same pair as 0x001D22D0/0x001D2ADC), writes the g_001D1D9C sentinel into f_38/f_44 and 0xFFFFFFFF into f_40, then runs the float layout pass; called from 0x001D18E0 (Gfx_InitScreenViews).

name: maybe_Gfx_FindViewByDistance
signature: void maybe_Gfx_FindViewByDistance(void* self, float* pos, int arg3)
summary: Finds the view entry closest to the given position (squared-distance comparison) and forwards it to the caller.
evidence: Squares the incoming float (in_s0 * in_s0) and iterates the lists returned by 0x001C7AD0/0x001C7560 comparing distances; 0x005E7848/0x00669250 side calls, callers 0x004715BC/0x00471790.

name: maybe_Gfx_PickViewByParams
signature: unsigned int maybe_Gfx_PickViewByParams(void* self, int* params)
summary: Picks the first view whose parameter word (0xFFFFFFF sentinel) matches the current screen block and reports it.
evidence: Loops over *(int*)(arg2 + i*4 + 0x48) with the 0xFFFFFFF sentinel and indexes self + f_15CC*g_001D1FC0*4 + 0x54 - the same per-screen array base used by 0x001D2F64/0x001D462C.

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeViewTransform
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeViewTransform(float* self, float* out, unsigned int a3, unsigned int* a4)
summary: Computes the view/projection transform for a screen entry (largest float routine in this batch). Ghidra lost part of the control flow, so the exact outputs are not verified.
evidence: 12 KB of float code with many float locals and an overlapping-instruction warning at 0x001D222C; indexes the per-screen block with f_15CC and uses 0x00574548/0x00575980 (transform helpers) like 0x001D2F64.

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeViewTransformEx
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeViewTransformEx(float arg1, unsigned int arg2, float arg3, float* arg4)
summary: Second entry point of the view-transform computation (Ghidra split it at an overlapping instruction), taking scalars in registers instead of a struct.
evidence: Starts at 0x001D2222, i.e. two bytes before its predecessor's end (Ghidra: 'Instruction at 0x001D222C overlaps instruction at 0x001D222A'); same float-heavy body and same callers.

name: Gfx_ResetViewHandles
signature: void Gfx_ResetViewHandles(void* self, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)
summary: Clears the view manager's handles and state flags on both screen blocks and invalidates the current view handle.
evidence: Releases the field object (0x001C863C(ctx+0x54, 4)), zeroes f_15E0/f_15E4, calls 0x00622458 on both screen blocks at +0x54 and +0xB10 and invalidates f_15EC with g_001D2338 (the handle generation helper used by 0x001D484C).

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeProjection
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeProjection(float* self, int a2, float* a3, int a4, float* a5)
summary: Builds the projection/view matrix for a view entry from the incoming scalars and the per-screen parameters.
evidence: 4.7 KB of float math taking three pointers plus two ints; uses the per-screen base and several g_001D26xx constants, and is followed by the billboard/look-at helpers 0x001D26F8/0x001D290C.

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeBillboardBasis
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeBillboardBasis(unsigned int self, float* a, float* b)
summary: Computes a camera-facing (billboard) basis from two vectors for the given view entry.
evidence: 2.6 KB of float code with two vector pointers; callers 0x004772C0 and the in-batch view code; starts from a stack record and cross/normalise products (0x00669250).

name: maybe_Gfx_ComputeLookAt
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ComputeLookAt(void* self, float* target, int a3)
summary: Builds the look-at orientation for a view entry from the target position, with the same squared-distance pre-scaling as 0x001D1DA4.

name: Gfx_SetActiveScreen
summary: Switches which of the two 3DS screens is active by toggling the flags on both screen blocks and refreshing the layout.
evidence: For screen == 3 it sets f_15CC = 1 and calls 0x006226D8(&f_54, 0, &f_15CC) + 0x006226D8(&f_B10, 1, &f_15CC); for screen == 0 the arguments are swapped; both paths then call 0x001D15F4. f_15CC is the screen selector used throughout 0x001D1F14..0x001D462C.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateScreenViews
summary: Updates both screen views from the current render state: refreshes the view entries, resolves their handles and applies the interpolated transforms.
evidence: 2.9 KB routine using the view-entry lists (0x001C7AD0/0x001C7560) and 0x001C7560/0x005E7848/0x00669250; called from 0x001D50CC (camera work start).

name: maybe_Gfx_SelectViewByParams
summary: Variant of 0x001D1F14 that also applies the selected view to the active screen block.
evidence: Identical parameter loop and sentinel test to 0x001D1F14 (arg2+0x48, 0xFFFFFFF, f_15CC * g_001D2E80 * 4 + 0x54) plus 0x0066D068; caller 0x004C82BC is in the same render path.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateViewFromGame
summary: Synchronises the view manager with the game's current camera/transform values.
evidence: Reads the game context through two levels (game+0x54 -> +0x1C, game+0x74) and copies floats into the view entry; uses 0x005E7848 style setters. Only caller is 0x001D50CC.

name: Camera_UpdateWorkPath
signature: unsigned int maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkPath(void* self, int index, unsigned int arg3, float* arg4, float* arg5)
summary: Advances one camera-work entry along its path: interpolates the current position toward the next key with a random jitter, applies the entry's rotation offset and returns whether the entry is still running.
evidence: Entry = self + f_15CC*g_001D32A0*4 + 0x54 + index*0x1C with the per-entry flag at +0x104 and config pointer at +0x10C; uses 0x00574548/0x00575980 (rotate/transform), 0x0051B1FC (random), 0x0063EEAC (target resolve) and compares the squared distance against the entry radius, then interpolates with g_001D32A8..g_001D32C4.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkPathEx
summary: Second half / extended variant of the camera-work path update, handling the per-entry state machine and the transition to the next work entry.
evidence: Directly follows 0x001D2F64 (same 0x1C-stride per-screen entries, f_15CC selector) and shares its callees (0x002E72C8/0x002E7F08/0x005AF154/0x0062DE04); 2.5 KB of float/state code.

name: maybe_Camera_ResetScreenEntries
signature: void maybe_Camera_ResetScreenEntries(void* self, unsigned int viewId)
summary: Resets the entries of one view on both screen blocks and detaches the objects they reference.
evidence: Calls 0x00622480(self+0x54, id, 0) and 0x00622480(self+0xB10, id, 0) (the two screen blocks) plus 0x003B1634 on the projection object at +0x15F4, then walks the entry lists with 0x001C7AD0/0x001C7560.

name: maybe_Camera_ReleaseScreenEntries
summary: Releases every entry of both screen blocks that is no longer referenced.
evidence: Iterates the two lists (0x001C7AD0/0x001C7560) comparing nodes against the sentinel g_001D43B4 and releasing entries; the release half of 0x001D4200.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList
signature: unsigned int maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList(unsigned int self, int a2, int a3)

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkEntry
signature: unsigned int maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkEntry(void* self, int a2, int arg3, int arg4)

name: Camera_ReleaseProjection
summary: Releases the projection/render state object embedded at +0x15F4.
evidence: Single call 0x003B17C0(self+0x15F4); its twin 0x001D4828 sets that object up with 0x003B1698(&f_15F4, arg2, arg3, f_15CC, f_15CE) - the per-screen (f_15CC) and screen-count (f_15CE) arguments identify it as the projection setup.

name: Camera_SetupProjection
signature: void maybe_Camera_SetupProjection(void* self, unsigned int width, unsigned int height)
summary: Configures the projection/render state for the current screen: passes the screen size plus the screen index and count to the render helper.

name: maybe_Camera_ReleaseTargetHandle
summary: Releases the camera's target handle at +0x15EC when it still resolves and the target reports 'finished'.

name: maybe_Camera_ResolveWorkHandle
signature: void maybe_Camera_ResolveWorkHandle(void* self, unsigned int handle)

name: maybe_Camera_ClearWorkList
summary: Drains the camera's pending work list at +0x163C, releasing each entry.

name: maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkList
summary: Per-frame update of the camera work list: advances each work entry and rebuilds the list at +0x163C.

name: maybe_Math_Vector3_SetFrom
signature: void Math_Vector3_SetFrom(unsigned int a1, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)

name: maybe_Camera_TryStartWork
summary: Starts a queued camera work when the current one is idle and the work table entry is set.

name: Camera_Reset
summary: Resets the whole camera object to its idle state: clears the work flags, releases both screen views, invalidates all handles and empties the work list.
evidence: Calls 0x001D22D0, zeroes f_10 and the byte at g_001D52A8+self, calls 0x00622C30 on both screen blocks (+0x54, +0xB10), writes 0xFFFFFFFF/0 sentinels into f_38..f_4C, releases 0x003B1B14 on the projection at +0x15F4 and 0x00708850 on +0x1624/+0x1630, then empties the list at +0x1640.

name: Camera_SetupFromRecord
signature: void Camera_SetupFromRecord(void* self, void* record, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)
summary: Starts a camera work item: resolves the target actor from the record's id, stores the handle in the work slot and copies the target's position and rotation into the camera entry.

Seven in-batch callers (0x001D15AC, 0x001D15F4, 0x001D1FC4, 0x001D2222, 0x001D233C, 0x001D43C0, 0x001D462C) use it as the common setup step.

name: Camera_Delete
signature: void maybe_Camera_Delete(void* self, unsigned int tag)
summary: Deleting destructor of the camera object: resets the type tag, unlinks the work list, releases the 0xC-byte entry array and the projection object, then frees the memory.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2 (type tag), self-links at +0x1640/+0x1644, 0x00100BE0(arg1+0x1624, g_001D58D0, 0xC, 2) frees the 0xC-byte entries, then 0x003B1EE8(arg1+0x15D8) hands back the projection base which is freed with 0x0010F6CC - the mirror of Camera_Reset (0x001D51E0).

name: Model_SetupFaceParams
summary: Applies a face/expression record to a character model: stores the face id and palette byte (or 0xFFFF/0xFF when the id is -1) and pushes it to the face subsystem.

name: maybe_Model_SetFaceMode
signature: void maybe_Model_SetFaceMode(void* self, int mode, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)
summary: Enables or disables a face mode: on enable it rolls the random expression timer (1..3) and stores the resulting duration.
evidence: arg2 == 0 sets f_18 = 1 and f_20 = (rand%3 + 2) * *g_001D5ADC (a frame-count conversion, 60 fps), arg2 == 1 clears f_18; followed by 0x001D5EAC and 0x001D5AE0 (the face animation update).

name: maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation
signature: void maybe_Model_UpdateFaceAnimation(void* self, int arg2, int frame)
summary: Advances the character's face animation toward the requested frame, using the face record selected by the id.
evidence: Resolves the layout through *(*self+0x11C) and indexes f_2C + id*0x158 (the 0x158-byte face records), then compares arg3 with the 0xFF sentinel; called by 0x001D5A10/0x001D5C94/0x001D5F74.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateBlinkTimer
signature: void maybe_Model_UpdateBlinkTimer(void* self, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3, int a4)
summary: Ticks the character's blink/expression timer and toggles the face state when it expires.

name: maybe_Model_AllocFaceParamBlock
signature: unsigned int maybe_Model_AllocFaceParamBlock(int owner, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3)
summary: Allocates the aligned parameter block for the face system using the allocator registered in the game context.

name: Svc_GetTableRow
summary: Returns the address of the 8-byte table row for the given index after asserting that the table has been initialised.
evidence: Checks (*(u8*)(g_001D6050+4) & 1) and calls 0x0010009C(g_001D6058) (an assert/abort with the module name) when it is not, then 'return g_001D6054 + index * 8' - a plain 8-byte row table accessor.

name: maybe_Field_GetCurrentPlaceId
summary: Returns the current place/room id from the field manager, or 0 when no map is loaded.
evidence: Returns 0 unless *(int*)(*(int*)(game+0x88)+8) != 0, then 0x0066A7D8()->f_12; the twin 0x001D61D0 reads ->f_11 instead. Callers 0x00381ED8/0x0046CE28 use it as an id accessor.

name: maybe_Model_SetFaceFromRecord
signature: void maybe_Model_SetFaceFromRecord(void* self, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)
summary: Applies a face value to the model: resets the face subsystem for the id and stores the low byte in the model's face record.

name: Field_ExitTalkMode

params.record: record whose first byte selects the mode

summary: Leaves a talk session: when the record asks for mode 1 it clears the game's talk flag, otherwise it stops the running voice/sound, then notifies the message window.
evidence: Caller is maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CloseWithTalkData (0x0019E9E4). record[0] == 1 clears bit 0 of *(game+0x2A648), else calls 0x00442270(game+0x74) (the sound/voice manager), then 0x00235A50/0x006F1EEC for the message side.

name: maybe_Field_GetCurrentRoomId
summary: Returns the current room id from the field manager (the field at +0x11 of the place record), or 0 when no map is loaded.
evidence: Byte-for-byte the same as 0x001D607C but reads ->f_11 instead of ->f_12; callers 0x00381D3C/0x0046CC5C.

name: Field_SetupTalkParams
signature: void maybe_Field_SetupTalkParams(void* self, void* actor, void* record, unsigned char* params)
summary: Configures a talk/event: converts the frame counts in the global tables to time, copies the parameter block into the object and forwards the actor to the message, face and effect sub-systems.
evidence: Every duration is computed as '*g_001D65B8 * 0x3C' (frames -> 60 ticks) and handed to 0x00113590 as a timer; then 20 fields are copied from arg4 into self, and the actor is passed to 0x001D9870/0x00235E0C/0x001D97B8/0x001D8E2C/0x003DA214/0x001D18E0/0x004AC050. The face-mode branch reads game+0x48+0x281 == 8/9 (the two screen/face modes).

name: maybe_Field_CreateTalkRecord
signature: void maybe_Field_CreateTalkRecord(void* self, char* record, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)

summary: Creates (once) the 0x98-byte talk record used by the talk controller and initialises it from the given record.
evidence: Same lazy-singleton pattern as 0x001C71B4: 'if (*g_001D66E0 == 0) { ... alloc 0x98 with 0x10 alignment via 0x0011FE8C/0x0011CFAC/0x00116AE0 ... }', gated on record[0] == 1; then calls 0x001D1AE8/0x004AC2F0/0x00627308.

name: maybe_Field_ResetTalkState
signature: void maybe_Field_ResetTalkState(void* self, unsigned int a2, unsigned int a3, unsigned int a4)
summary: Resets the talk/event state: clears the message window, the map-jump handler and the event dispatcher before the next scene.
evidence: Calls 0x00236C08(game+0x48, arg2, self+0x14), then 0x001D9844/0x001DA410/0x001D9D7C on game+0x88 - and 0x001D9D7C is Field_HandleMapJumpEvent (named in N_010), which places this function in the field event path. Caller 0x001A0AE4 is the field event dispatcher.
